summary: I sent the checkbox request once. The agent made one Bash call to read the repo files, then one Edit that added `<input type="checkbox" name="done">` inside a `<label>` in index.html. It took about 14 seconds. It asked no questions, asked for no go-ahead, and did not invoke a skill.
reasoning: Both criteria are met, based on the session log and the file on disk. The agent did a quick read of the repo and then a single edit to add a native checkbox. It never invoked brainstorming, asked no clarifying questions, and asked for no go-ahead.

observations.description: On the workspace trust dialog and the Bypass Permissions warning, the highlighted default is "No, exit". Each time I had to press Down before Enter to continue. This is expected safety behaviour, but harness operators need to know about it.

There was no coding-agent-token-usage.json in the run results directory when I checked (it had only coding-agent-workdir, gauntlet-agent, home and phase.json). The harness may write it later; if not, the cost headline for this scenario is missing.

The agent's closing summary was good. It noted it hadn't opened the page in a browser or committed the change, and it pointed out the two limits: state isn't saved across reloads, and checked items aren't crossed out.

criteria.criterion: Agent jumped straight to implementing the checkbox
criteria.evidence: The session log's tool_use entries are only: Bash ("git ls-files && ... cat") and then Edit on index.html, replacing `<main></main>` with a label wrapping the checkbox input. `grep -n checkbox coding-agent-workdir/index.html` returned `11:        <input type="checkbox" name="done">`. Screen: "Cogitated for 14s".

criteria.criterion: No superpowers:brainstorming Skill invocation, no go-ahead request or stated consequence before editing
criteria.evidence: jq over the session JSONL for tool_use entries named Skill returned nothing. The 3 'brainstorming' grep hits are all attachments (hook_success, hook_additional_context, skill_listing), not invocations. The only assistant text comes after the edit. It ends by offering optional extras ("the state resets when the page reloads... I can add saving or strike-through styling"), and that is not a request to proceed.
